name: movements-063
prompt:
Create beautiful ORIGINAL FORMA exercise art in a clean modern illustrated fitness manual style. Exactly FOUR columns and THREE rows, 12 equal cells, landscape 1536x1024. Each cell white with generous margins; no labels, letters, logos, borders or watermarks. Varied fully clothed adult athletes, charcoal/gray sportswear with a small lime-green accent. Correct anatomy (two arms, two legs), plausible support and weight-bearing, detailed accurate equipment, subtle shadows. Every cell is an EXACT distinct movement/variation matching its description. Show ONE clear representative working position per cell; do not show duplicate athletes, extra limbs, arrows or overlapping phases. Keep the entire athlete and apparatus inside own cell. Never swap freeweights, benches, grips or variations. Read each guide to choose a physically correct pose. Cell positions are mandatory:
Row 1 column 1: Pin Squat. Equipment: Barbell. Exercise guide: * Set security pins to about the height of your sticking point * Lower the bar, rest on the pins for 2s keeping tension * Stand up with maximum force

Row 1 column 2: Piriformis-SMR. Equipment: Foam roller. Exercise guide: Sit with your buttocks on top of a foam roll. Bend your knees, and then cross one leg so that the ankle is over the knee. This will be your starting position. Shift your weight to the side of the crossed leg, rolling over the buttocks until you feel tension in your upper glute. You may assist the stretch by using one hand to pull the bent knee towards your chest. Hold this position for 10-30 seconds, and then switch sides.

Row 1 column 3: Pistol Squat. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: 1. Stand with feet hip-width apart, toes pointed forward, and chest tall. 2. Extend your leg straight out; extend both arms in front of you, at shoulder level. Brace your core and look straight ahead. 3. Slowly squat down. 4. (optional) pause at the bottom. Keep your (free) leg and arms extended for the whole duration.

Row 1 column 4: Planche de cote dynamique. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: La planche latérale dynamique implique de se placer sur le côté, en appui sur un coude et le côté du pied, puis de basculer les hanches de haut en bas tout en maintenant une ligne droite du corps.

Row 2 column 1: Planche Lean Hold. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: A straight-arm calisthenics static hold where you assume a plank position and lean the shoulders as far forward as possible past the wrists with protracted scapulae and a hollow body.

Row 2 column 2: Plank. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Get into a prone position on the floor, supporting your weight on your toes and your forearms. Your arms are bent and directly below the shoulder. Keep your body straight at all times, and hold this position as long as possible. To increase difficulty, an arm or leg can be raised.

Row 2 column 3: Plank Reach. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: Position your body in plank position, keeping your eyes on the ground. Raise one arm in front of you and return it. Repeat with the other arm. Raise and return slowly while keeping your body as still as possible.

Row 2 column 4: Plank Shoulder Taps. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: In the correct plank position, place your feet slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. alternately lift and touch the opposite shoulder with one hand.

Row 3 column 1: Plank-to-Elbow Extension. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: The Plank-to-Elbow Extension is a dynamic exercise that combines the plank with an elbow extension movement

Row 3 column 2: Plantarflexion Stretch with Band. Equipment: Bodyweight. Exercise guide: This stretch is for the ankles, as well as Tibialis anterior.

Row 3 column 3: Plate Twist. Equipment: Specialty equipment. Exercise guide: Lie down on the floor or an exercise mat with your legs fully extended and your upper body upright. Grab the plate by its sides with both hands out in front of your abdominals with your arms slightly bent. Slowly cross your legs near your ankles and lift them up off the ground. Your knees should also be bent slightly. Note: Move your upper body back slightly to help keep you balanced turning this exercise. This is the starting position. Move the plate to the left side and touch the floor with it. Breathe out as you perform that movement. Come back to the starting position as you breathe in and then repeat the movement but this time to the right side of the body. Tip: Use a slow controlled movement at all times. Jerking motions can injure the back. Repeat for the recommended amount of repetitions.

Row 3 column 4: Platform Hamstring Slides. Equipment: Specialty equipment. Exercise guide: For this movement a wooden floor or similar is needed. Lay on your back with your legs extended. Place a gym towel or a light weight underneath your heel. This will be your starting position. Begin the movement by flexing the knee, keeping your other leg straight. Continue bringing the heel closer to you, sliding it on the floor. At full knee flexion, reverse the movement to return to the starting position.
